chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Criminal offenses and penalties
paragraphs: (a) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly and willfully assaults, resists, opposes, impedes, intimidates, or interferes with an officer of the Capitol Police, a special officer of the Capitol Police, or any person assisting the Capitol Police while such officer or person is engaged in the performance of official duties under this Act.

(b) A person who violates the preceding paragraph shall be fined not more than $2,500, imprisoned for not more than three days, or both. If the violation involves physical contact, bodily injury, use of a weapon, threat of serious bodily injury, or conduct creating a substantial risk of harm, the person shall be fined not more than $7,500, imprisoned for not more than seven days, or both.
(c) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly enters or remains in any restricted area of the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds without lawful authority.

(d) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly enters or remains in a House-controlled area, Senate-controlled area, chamber floor, gallery, committee room, secured office, restricted corridor, emergency perimeter, or temporary restricted area after being denied entry, ordered to leave, or informed that such area is restricted.

(e) A person who violates either of the two preceding paragraphs shall be fined not more than $1,500, imprisoned for not more than two days, or both. If the violation occurs during a congressional proceeding, emergency, lockdown, evacuation, joint session, chamber proceeding, committee proceeding, or major security event, the person shall be fined not more than $5,000, imprisoned for not more than five days, or both.

(f) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly and willfully obstructs, impedes, disrupts, or attempts to obstruct, impede, or disrupt the orderly conduct of congressional business, a chamber proceeding, a committee proceeding, a hearing, a vote, a joint session, an investigation, an official ceremony, or any other official function of Congress or either House.

(g) A person who violates the preceding paragraph shall be fined not more than $3,000, imprisoned for not more than three days, or both. If the obstruction involves violence, threat of violence, forced entry, property damage, intimidation of a Member of Congress, officer of Congress, witness, employee, or invited guest, or interference with a vote or official proceeding, the person shall be fined not more than $7,500, imprisoned for not more than seven days, or both.

(h) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly fails to comply with a lawful order of an officer of the Capitol Police, a special officer of the Capitol Police, the Chief, the Board, a Sergeant at Arms, a Presiding Officer, or another officer acting under lawful authority to leave an area, cease disruptive conduct, submit to lawful screening, remain outside a restricted area, comply with an emergency measure, or stop interfering with congressional business.
(i) A person who violates the preceding paragraph shall be fined not more than $1,000, imprisoned for not more than two days, or both.

(j) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly and falsely represents himself or herself to be an officer of the Capitol Police, a special officer of the Capitol Police, an employee of the Capitol Police, a Sergeant at Arms, an employee of either Sergeant at Arms, or any person authorized to exercise security authority under this Act.

(k) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly uses, displays, manufactures, transfers, possesses, alters, or attempts to use any false, stolen, expired, revoked, altered, or unauthorized badge, credential, access card, pass, identification, uniform, insignia, vehicle marking, or security device for the purpose of gaining access, avoiding screening, influencing an officer, impersonating authority, or entering a restricted area.

(l) A person who violates either of the two preceding paragraphs shall be fined not more than $3,000, imprisoned for not more than three days, or both. If the violation is committed to enter a restricted area, approach a protected person, obstruct congressional business, commit another offense, or facilitate a threat against Congress, the person shall be fined not more than $7,500, imprisoned for not more than seven days, or both. (m)A person commits an offense if such person knowingly makes a false threat, false report, or false statement concerning a bomb, weapon, hazardous material, active threat, fire, attack, assassination threat, security breach, or other emergency affecting the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, a Member of Congress, an officer of Congress, a congressional employee, a witness, an invited guest, a congressional proceeding, or an official function of Congress.
(n) A person who violates the preceding paragraph shall be fined not more than $10,000, imprisoned for not more than seven days, or both.

(o) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly damages, destroys, defaces, tampers with, disables, obstructs, removes, or interferes with any barrier, camera, alarm, lock, screening device, communication device, access control device, emergency equipment, protective equipment, official vehicle, security post, record, document, badge, credential, or other property used by the Capitol Police or either Sergeant at Arms for the protection of Congress.

(p) A person who violates the preceding paragraph shall be fined not more than $3,000, imprisoned for not more than three days, or both. If the violation creates a substantial risk of injury, compromises an emergency response, assists unlawful entry, obstructs a congressional proceeding, or occurs during an emergency, the person shall be fined not more than $7,500, imprisoned for not more than seven days, or both.

(q) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly threatens, intimidates, harasses, obstructs, or attempts to influence a Member of Congress, officer of Congress, congressional employee, witness, invited guest, officer of the Capitol Police, special officer, or employee of the Capitol Police because of such person’s official duties, testimony, vote, debate, service, employment, appearance, cooperation, security action, or participation in congressional business.
(r) A person who violates the preceding paragraph shall be fined not more than $10,000, imprisoned for not more than seven days, or both.
(s) A person commits an offense if such person knowingly aids, abets, commands, induces, procures, assists, or conspires with another person to commit an offense under this section.
(t) A person who violates the preceding paragraph shall be subject to the same maximum penalty authorized for the underlying offense.
(u) An offense under this section may be investigated by the Capitol Police and referred to the Department of Justice or another lawful prosecuting authority.

(v) The penalties provided in this section shall not limit prosecution under any other applicable law. A person may be charged under this section, under another applicable criminal statute, or under both, where the same conduct violates more than one law. (w)A court imposing a sentence under this section may impose imprisonment, a fine, probation, community service, restitution, a stay-away order, a restriction from the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, or any other lawful condition appropriate to the offense.

(x) A fine imposed under this section shall be paid in the manner provided by law and may be considered in addition to restitution for damaged property, emergency costs, or other losses caused by the offense.
